title: Undrained Shear Strength from Vane Torque
applicability: Assumes uniform shear stress distribution on cylindrical failure surface (sides + top + bottom). For standard vane H/D = 2: Su = 6T/(7πD³). Exact only for isotropic shear strength; actual failure surface has variable mobilization.

title: Sensitivity from Vane Test

St.description: Sensitivity (ratio of peak to remolded undrained shear strength)

Su(peak).description: Peak undrained shear strength from first rotation

Su(remolded).description: Remolded undrained shear strength after 10+ full revolutions

applicability: St < 2: insensitive. 2–4: medium. 4–8: sensitive. 8–16: extra-sensitive. > 16: quick. Quick clays (St > 30) undergo complete strength loss when remolded.

title: Bjerrum Correction Factor

Su(design).description: Corrected undrained shear strength for stability analysis

applicability: PI = 20: μ ≈ 1.0. PI = 50: μ ≈ 0.78. PI = 75: μ ≈ 0.69. PI = 100: μ ≈ 0.62. Aas et al. (1986) refined using OCR and PI. Always apply for slope stability; not needed for bearing capacity (which has its own factors).

title: Vane Torque with Anisotropic Shear Strength
equation: T = π × D² × [H/2 × Su(H) + D/6 × Su(V)]

Su(H).description: Undrained shear strength on horizontal planes (sides of cylinder)

Su(V).description: Undrained shear strength on vertical planes (top and bottom)

applicability: For H/D = 2 standard vane: T ≈ π×D³/6 × [2×Su(H) + Su(V)]/3. The measured Su is a weighted average of horizontal and vertical strength. In anisotropic clays, Su(H)/Su(V) can be 1.5–2.0. Wroth (1984) provides framework for separating components using different H/D vanes.

title: Rate Correction for Non-Standard Rotation

Su(ref).description: Shear strength corrected to reference rotation rate

Su(test).description: Measured shear strength at test rotation rate

applicability: Su increases approximately 5–10% per log cycle of strain rate. Exponent 0.05 is approximate; varies with soil type. If test performed at non-standard rate, apply correction.

title: Su/σ'v0 Ratio from Vane (SHANSEP Check)

S.description: Normally consolidated Su/σ'v0 ratio (0.20–0.25 for most clays from FVT)

applicability: Plot Su(FVT)/σ'v0 vs. depth to assess consistency with expected OCR profile. Values significantly above trend may indicate desiccation, cementation, or test error. Values below may indicate sample disturbance or drainage during test.
